material_definitions: The material series investigated is Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, focusing on aliovalent substitution of Ge for P.
The structure and properties were analyzed using X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance.
Increasing Ge content induces anion site disorder and significantly drops the activation barrier for ionic motion.

material_definitions: The class of argyrodites Li6PS5X (X = Cl, Br, I) has attracted considerable interest.
If iodine is the halide in the structure, no site-disorder occurs due to the large size mismatch between S2– and I–.
Kraft et al. found that the absence of disorder in iodine containing argyrodites is associated with high activation barriers and low ionic conductivity.
warnings: Temperature inferred as 25 C (room temperature) since no explicit value was given.

material_definitions: The effect of Ge4+ substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I (argyrodite structure) was investigated to tailor structure-transport relationships.
Increasing Ge-fraction induces site disorder between the S2– and I– positions and expands the diffusion pathways for Li+.
This structural change correlates to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and an increase in conductivity.
This approach achieved the highest lithium argyrodites reported so far, with values reaching 18.4 mS cm-1 upon sintering.
warnings: Temperature inferred as 25 C (room temperature) since no explicit value was given.
The specific value of 'x' corresponding to this maximum conductivity is not explicitly stated.
Uncertainty (± 0.8) ignored.

material_definitions: The Li+ superionic argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I were synthesized with increasing Ge4+/P5+ ratios.
Full solid solutions can be synthesized up to a composition of at least Li6.7P0.3Ge0.7S5I.
Samples generally exhibit minor impurity phase fractions of LiI and/or Li4GeS4.
warnings: Temperature (298 K) is inferred as room temperature based on typical experimental practice and context provided in Figure 5a caption.

The materials exhibit interpenetration of face-centered cubic lattices.

Structural changes and increasing I


/S2


 site-disorder lead to opening of bottlenecks and more facile inter-cage jumps, dropping the activation barrier.
